narrative.intro: Battelle Memorial Institute obligated $140M in federal contract funding in FY2027 to date. Battelle received 1 award so far in the fiscal year, with an average award size of $140M. Obligations fell 91.4% year over year. Prior fiscal years show much larger annual obligations: FY22 at $1.5B, FY23 at $1.6B, FY24 at $1.6B, FY25 at $1.6B, and FY26 at $1.6B. The current-year total is a fiscal year to date figure and other tables in this report use total contract values for award and expiring-contract entries where noted. The 1 award driving FY2027 obligations is large relative to the typical yearly totals this vendor posted from FY22 through FY26. Contractors and program managers tracking Battelle should note the sharp year-over-year decline in obligations for the current fiscal year to date when comparing FY2027 to prior full-year totals, and should treat the FY2027 figure as partial until the fiscal year closes.

sections.heading: Why are FY2027 obligations so much lower than prior years?
sections.body: The FY2027 to date obligations for Battelle Memorial Institute are $140M, down 91.4% year over year. Prior full-year obligations were $1.5B in FY22 and $1.6B in each of FY23, FY24, FY25, and FY26. The FY2027 total is a fiscal year to date figure, which explains much of the difference versus prior full-year totals. The single award in FY2027 accounts for the entire current-year obligations.

sections.heading: How should contractors interpret the single large award in FY2027?
sections.body: The single award in FY2027 has an average award size of $140M, which equals total FY2027 obligations of $140M. Prior years show many more obligations at multi-hundred-million to billion-dollar annual levels. A single large award can skew year-to-date comparisons and does not by itself indicate a long-term shift in vendor capacity or market share. Treat FY2027 as partial and monitor subsequent obligations for a fuller picture.
